title: Avoiding the Reverse Fall Trap in Drainage Piping
description: One of the most frequent errors in drainage installation is failing to maintain consistent downward slope, leading to 'reverse fall' or negative pitch. When a drain pipe sags or slopes upward against the direction of flow, wastewater pools inside the pipe instead of discharging fully. Over time, these stagnant pools collect solid waste, grease, and debris, rapidly forming severe clogs. Professional installation requires verifying grade continuously using proper alignment tools and adequate support hangers to prevent pipe deflection under load. Learning to spot and correct incorrect pitches during rough-in saves countless callbacks and ensures long-term system reliability.
